[MUQATIL:40:25-28/r4] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Pharaoh's words mean let me kill Moses and let Moses's Lord protect him from being killed.
[MUQATIL:40:25-28/r5] MUQATIL, d. 150 · فرعون | reports | Pharaoh says he fears Moses will change their religion, meaning their worship of Pharaoh.
[MUQATIL:40:25-28/r6] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The land is Egypt; Pharaoh calls it corruption if Moses kills their sons and spares their women as they had done to his people.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيركلاسمكانتعينهواواوكانتالعينثانيةأوثالثة)#622/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A root wāw as the second radical remains in the diminutive because it is mobile, as in لوزة، جوزة، and قولة.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيركلاسمكانتعينهواواوكانتالعينثانيةأوثالثة)#622/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | prefers | A root wāw as the third radical normally changes to yāʾ in the diminutive; Sībawayh calls this the better form because a preceding diminutive yāʾ pulls the wāw toward yāʾ.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيركلاسمكانتعينهواواوكانتالعينثانيةأوثالثة)#622/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · بعض العرب | reports | Some Arabs retain the wāw in the cited third-radical forms, but Sībawayh calls this the less preferred alternative.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيركلاسمكانتعينهواواوكانتالعينثانيةأوثالثة)#622/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Those who preserve wāw in أسيود do not extend that preservation to مقام and مقال as مقيوم and مقيول; if the wāw appeared, the expected rule would change it.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيركلاسمكانتعينهواواوكانتالعينثانيةأوثالثة)#622/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | An added third-radical wāw, as in جدول and قسور, may remain in the diminutive because it is a live consonant and is retained in the plural.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيركلاسمكانتعينهواواوكانتالعينثانيةأوثالثة)#622/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Al-Farazdaq's قساور للقسور الأصيد attests the plural that retains the added wāw of قسور.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيركلاسمكانتعينهواواوكانتالعينثانيةأوثالثة)#622/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A final root wāw does not remain in the diminutive; it weakens to yāʾ, as in غزوة، رضوى، and عشواء.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيركلاسمكانتعينهواواوكانتالعينثانيةأوثالثة)#622/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The wāw in عجوز and جزور is only vowel lengthening, never a stable radical; because it also disappears in their broken plural, it cannot remain in the diminutive.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيركلاسمكانتعينهواواوكانتالعينثانيةأوثالثة)#622/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | معاوية permits retention like أسود because its wāw belongs to the root, was originally mobile, and remains in the plural, unlike the wāw of عجوز.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماكانفيهقلب)#621/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A lexicalized metathesis is retained in the diminutive rather than restored to its etymological order, as in قائل and other established forms.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماكانفيهقلب)#621/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Al-ʿAjjāj's لاث derives from لائث by moving wāw after thāʾ; Ṭarīf b. Tamīm's شاك similarly represents الشائك with the segments transposed.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماكانفيهقلب)#621/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Sībawayh gives أينق from أنوق and القسي from القووس as further lexicalized reversals, with the changed order retained in their derived forms.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماكانفيهقلب)#621/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Al-Khalil derives مسائيك from المساءة by metathesis; Kaʿb b. Malik's سآها and Kuthayyir ʿAzza's راءني illustrate the same pattern in poetry.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماكانفيهقلب)#621/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Sībawayh also analyzes راءني as رآني with the hamza moved and reports Abu al-Khattab's variant راءة for راية; a line by Hassan b. Thabit illustrates alif replacing hamza.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتسميةالمذكربلفظالاثنينوالجميعالذيتلحقلهالواحدواوا#537/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | prefers | When رجلان is used as a man's name, Sībawayh prefers preserving the dual declension: رجلان in the nominative and رجلين in the oblique cases.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتسميةالمذكربلفظالاثنينوالجميعالذيتلحقلهالواحدواوا#537/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · من النحويين | reports | Some grammarians treat the name رجلان like عثمان rather than declining it as a regular dual.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتسميةالمذكربلفظالاثنينوالجميعالذيتلحقلهالواحدواوا#537/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Al-Khalil extends the dual-like nominative رجلان to oblique رجلين, analogizing the ending to سنين and dialectal فلسطين and قنسرين; رجلين is not used as nominative because this form otherwise lacks a nominal parallel.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتسميةالمذكربلفظالاثنينوالجميعالذيتلحقلهالواحدواوا#537/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Names ending in feminine plural -āt remain declinable: in oblique cases their tāʾ resembles the yāʾ of مسلمِين, and tanwīn functions like its nūn.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتسميةالمذكربلفظالاثنينوالجميعالذيتلحقلهالواحدواوا#537/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The proper name عرفات is declined and takes no definite article, showing that it is definite despite its -āt ending.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتسميةالمذكربلفظالاثنينوالجميعالذيتلحقلهالواحدواوا#537/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · بعض العرب | reports | Some Arabs omit tanwīn from أذرعات and compare its ending to feminine -ah; Sībawayh cites an Imruʾ al-Qays line and explains that the intervening alif is not a strong barrier.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابكينونتهافيالأسماء)#724/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A small class of nouns has hamzat al-waṣl, including ابن، اثنان، امرؤ، ابنم، اسم، and است; feminine forms add tāʾ, as in ابنة، اثنتان، and امرأة.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابكينونتهافيالأسماء)#724/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | These nouns take kasra on initial hamzat al-waṣl even when the third vowel is ḍamma, since that ḍamma is not stable; verbs with a stable third ḍamma differ.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابكينونتهافيالأسماء)#724/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Hamzat al-waṣl is generally dropped after connected speech, except the alif of the article in a question and أيمن in an oath, where deletion could confuse it with the interrogative hamza.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابكينونتهافيالأسماء)#724/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Poets may restart hamzat al-waṣl after a pause or hemistich break; Sībawayh cites lines by an unnamed poet and Labīd as examples.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابكينونتهافيالأسماء)#724/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Frequent clitic combinations can suppress the vowel of hāʾ in هو and هي after و، ف، or ل, and of imperative lām after و or ف; some Arabs retain the original vowels.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Nouns with a radical final yāʾ or wāw preceded by kasra or ḍamma lose that weak letter in inflection and retain a preceding kasra.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | A man named قاض keeps the same inflection as the form had before becoming a proper name.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | holds | A man named جوار has the same nominative and genitive forms as before proper naming; its diptote pattern would resist declension more strongly than قاض.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | holds | A woman named جوار takes tanwīn because here tanwīn compensates for the deleted yāʾ, as in أذرعات.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | A woman named قاض is declinable in the nominative and genitive; the same pattern applies to a man named أدل.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | holds | A man named أعمى keeps the ordinary diminutive أعيم; أفعل comparatives can take tanwīn in contexts such as خير منك.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · يونس | rejects | Yūnus decides whether a defective proper name is diptote by comparing its sound counterpart as a definite noun, so he says جواري and مررت بجواري.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r16] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | rejects | Al-Khalīl rejects Yūnus's rule: if the name followed its sound counterpart, speakers would keep the same nominative and genitive behavior and use the accusative in the indefinite genitive pattern too.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r17] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | prefers | Al-Khalīl treats tanwīn as a stable substitute for the deleted yāʾ; he rejects a woman's name قاضي retaining yāʾ in the genitive.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r18] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Poetic necessity can restore weak endings in inflection: the Hudhalī poet has معاري, al-Farazdaq مواليا, and Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt and Jarīr supply further forced forms.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r19] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Further poetic necessity restores original forms, including يعيليا and سمائيا; the line ألم يأتيك also restores a jussive ending, and al-Kumayt forces ضننوا.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In nominative and genitive, the deleted yāʾ is compensated for by tanwīn, making these forms declinable.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r20] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | A man named يرمي or أرمي takes tanwīn, as do the comparable feminine-name forms قاض and أعيم.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r21] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | When a man is named غزو, the inflected form is غزي: retaining wāw after ḍamma belongs to verbs, not nouns; the verse about القلنسي supports the noun pattern.

[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r26] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A name taken from a jussive clause with لم must preserve the governing construction; where the weak ending is moved, it becomes visible as in يريد and يخاف.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r27] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Naming the doubled imperative أعضض yields إعض: the initial hamza is cut and the doubled consonants assimilate, as in the verb pattern أعض.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r28] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The form ألبب remains on its original pattern, like رجاء ابن حيوة and ضيون; Arabic sometimes preserves the source form despite a different usual pattern.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In accusative, inflect a defective form according to whether its sound counterpart is declinable or diptote.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | An extra final yāʾ or wāw preceded by its matching vowel behaves like a radical weak ending.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Examples of a radical yāʾ preceded by kasra include قاض, غاز, مغاز, and جوار; forms preceded by ḍamma include أدل and أظب.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | For an added wāw preceded by ḍamma, he gives the plural عرق for عرقوة and a rajaz line containing عرقي.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A weak ending preceded by fatḥa becomes alif; it is not deleted in pause, and its tanwīn behavior otherwise follows sound nouns.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The diptote forms عذارى and صحارى take no tanwīn because their final alif completes the mafāʿil pattern.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماينصرفومالاينصرفمنبناتالياءوالواوالتيالياءات#553/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A final yāʾ or wāw preceded by a consonant with sukūn behaves like a sound ending, as in ظبي and دلو.
[SIBAWAYH:ولاms339علامةالمضمرالمتكلمولاعلامةالمضمرالمحدثعنهالغائبوذلكأنه#422/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | For ordinary action verbs, an attached object pronoun cannot be reflexive when subject and object are identical; speakers say اقتل نفسك instead. The verse's separate object موسى is not that case.
[SIBAWAYH:ولاms339علامةالمضمرالمتكلمولاعلامةالمضمرالمحدثعنهالغائبوذلكأنه#422/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Reflexive clitics are possible with verbs of belief and judgment because these take a subject-predicate complement like إنّ; رأى of physical sight remains a simple action verb, while mental رأى patterns with them.
[ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p180#5/r1] ABDURRAZZAQ, d. 211 · قتادة | reports | Qatāda says Pharaoh called the guidance Moses brought “corruption” in the land.
[ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p180#5/r2] ABDURRAZZAQ, d. 211 · مجاهد | reports | Mujāhid is reported to have recited the clause as “and that he should cause corruption to appear in the land.”
[IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r5] IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB, d. 276 · author | holds | Āmīn is a name of God and a prayer response said after al-Fātiḥa; some exegetes derive it from a shortened “O God, answer me,” with the vocative omitted.
[IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r6] IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB, d. 276 · أصحاب اللغة | prefers | Language scholars prefer short-alif Amīn: they open it because it stands alone from its implicit vocative sense and has come to mean “so may God do.”
[IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r7] IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB, d. 276 · فطحل | reports | The poet Faṭḥal’s verse with Amīn supports the short-vowelled form preferred by the language scholars.
[IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r8] IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB, d. 276 · قوم فصحاء | reports | Ibn Qutayba also records the long-alif form Āmīn from eloquent speakers.
[IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r9] IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB, d. 276 · author | holds | The long form is traced to yā Amīn, “O God”; the initial yāʾ was dropped for ease because the expression is frequent, like yā Zayd becoming ā Zayd, and related forms heard from eloquent Arabs.
[TAB-FULL:v20p308/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Pharaoh tells his court to let him kill Moses and let Moses call the Lord he claims sent him to protect him; Pharaoh says Moses will change their religion by his magic.
[TAB-FULL:v20p308/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · قراء المدينة والشام والبصرة | reports | Most readers in Medina, Syria, and Basra read وأن without an alif, as in the Medinan codices.
[TAB-FULL:v20p308/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · قراء الكوفة | reports | Most Kufan readers read أو أن with an alif, as in their codices, and read يظهر with a fatḥa on yāʾ and الفساد in the nominative. | mentions 11:87
[TAB-FULL:v20p308/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Al-Tabari accepts both widespread conjunction readings as close in meaning: whether corruption is made manifest or appears, an agent's manifestation is implicit.
[TAB-FULL:v20p308/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Pharaoh feared Moses would change their religion or openly establish worship of his Lord in Egypt, which Pharaoh considered corruption; replacing their religion with its opposite amounted to making corruption appear.
[TAB-FULL:v20p308/r6] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · قتادة | reports | Qatada glosses their religion as the affair or condition they currently follow.

[ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r2] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | With aw, Pharaoh presents alternatives: he fears Moses will abolish the religion, or, if not abolish it, corrupt it; Pharaoh calls obedience to God corruption.

[IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r1] IBNMUJAHID, d. 324 · ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر | reports | These readers read وأن يظهر without an alif before the conjunction.
[IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r2] IBNMUJAHID, d. 324 · عاصم وحمزة والكسائي | reports | Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisai read أو أن يظهر with an alif before the conjunction; this form also appears in Kufan codices.
[IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r3] IBNMUJAHID, d. 324 · نافع وأبو عمرو | reports | Nafi and Abu Amr read يظهر with a ḍamma on the yāʾ and الفساد in the accusative.
[IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r4] IBNMUJAHID, d. 324 · ابن كثير وابن عامر | reports | Ibn Kathir and Ibn Amir read يظهر with the yāʾ described as منصوب and الفساد in the nominative.
[IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r5] IBNMUJAHID, d. 324 · عاصم فى رواية أبى بكر وحمزة والكسائى | reports | Asim in Abu Bakr's transmission, Hamza, and al-Kisai read يظهر with an open yāʾ and الفساد in the nominative.
[IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r6] IBNMUJAHID, d. 324 · حفص عن عاصم | reports | Hafs from Asim reads يظهر with a ḍamma on the yāʾ and الفساد in the accusative.
